parts.note_add: The 1981-83 factory ACV holds three valves in one body - the air relief valve, the air switching valve and the No.1 anti-afterburn valve - and is not repairable: it is replaced as a unit (S-006 p72-73, 1981). A block-off plate for 81-91 non-turbo engines (Racing Beat 16325, sold by Atkins Rotary) exists if the air injection has been removed.

The 1981-82 system has two check valves: one for port air (ACV to exhaust port) and one for split air (ACV to the 2-bed catalyst); this part (1480-13-730, figure 1371A-1) is the one on the ACV (S-006 p71-72).

The shutter valve on the intake manifold shuts the rear primary port on deceleration while the combined coasting valve lets fresh air into the rear primary port; its diaphragm is worked by manifold vacuum through the yellow-dot shutter solenoid valve, active on deceleration above about 1100 rpm (S-006 p78, p94-95).

Five three-way vacuum solenoid valves, each coded by a coloured dot: air-con/throttle opener white, air relief blue, coasting/shutter yellow, air switching gray, vacuum control (distributor advance cut) orange (S-006 p85). The 1982 wiring diagram feeds each from the emission control unit, with the other pin to ground (S-001 p12).

The 1981 layout's vacuum-driven pieces are the shutter valve diaphragm, the throttle opener (pulls the throttle open with the A/C on), two choke diaphragms, the dash pot (M/T) and the distributor advance units (S-006 p66, p93-95); which of them this 'actuator' 3648-13-290 is, the catalogue does not say - check on the car.
This is the No.2 anti-afterburn valve (the No.1 is inside the air control valve): on the first moment of deceleration it lets air from the air cleaner into the rear secondary port (S-006 p77, p95).

The 1981 vacuum routing shows the delay valve in the vacuum line to the No.1 choke diaphragm, which it lets pull the choke further open a few seconds after start (S-006 p82, p108); check that this is where it sits on the car.
New 8871-14-700A is no longer available (Atkins Rotary lists it NLA, 79-82 12A); the thermo pellet PT199 comes fitted in new coolers.
Atkins Rotary sells 8871-14-810 new (Mazda, with crush washer) as fitting all 1979-91 RX-7s, which confirms the catalogue's unreadable digit as 14.
Available new as the 79-82 12A short oil cooler line (Atkins Rotary, Mazda 1011-14-720); a steel-braided line kit (Atkins 11907) also exists for 79-82 12A.
Available new as the 79-82 12A long oil cooler line (Atkins Rotary, Mazda 8871-14-730).

The 1982 wiring diagram shows three temperature switches on the emission control unit: No.1 water temp switch B-12 (engine, LB/LW, on below 70 C), No.2 water temp switch B-11 (radiator, LB/LY, on above 15 C) and the heat hazard sensor B-13 (floor, LB/RY, 130 C) (S-001 p12; S-006 p85, p93-94); which of them the two 18 890 thermo switches are is not stated - check on the car.

Senses throttle opening, radiator temperature, choke knob, floor temperature and engine speed (from the ignition coil primary), and drives the five three-way solenoids and the heat hazard lamp; its speed switch points are 1100 and 4000 rpm (S-006 p70, p85, p93).
This is the 2-bed pellet rear converter: split air from the air control valve is injected between its two beds; a heat hazard sensor under the floor lights the overheat lamp (S-006 p69, p71).
The Mazda pipe 1480-40-200 is discontinued; Racing Beat's stainless connecting pipe 16204 (81-83) is the listed replacement.
Replacement: Racing Beat Power Pulse muffler 16433 for 1981-82 RX-7 ($519.75 at Mazdatrix; no gaskets or hangers).
Hanger rubber 1114-40-160 is available new (Atkins Rotary, fits 79-91 RX-7), superseding 0820-40-161 and 1114-40-161.
